mainEntity.name: Can it tell an emergency from a Monday job?

acceptedAnswer.text: It asks the questions you give it: is water running now, is anyone without water, can the caller reach a shutoff. Active leaks and no-water calls get the next opening or a transfer to your on-call number; a slow drain or a dripping faucet gets the next regular slot. You set the rules, and you can read every transcript to check them.

Only what you tell it to. If you give it a trip fee or an after-hours rate, it will say that and nothing else. It never invents a number. Anything outside what you approved becomes a message, and the caller gets a text back so the lead stays warm.

mainEntity.name: What if I want to take the call myself?

acceptedAnswer.text: Then take it. The agent picks up only what you cannot: the calls you miss, the calls after hours, the calls that come in while you are under a house. Most 24-hour shops we talk to answer their own phone and want to keep it that way. The agent is the backstop, not the replacement.
